<li><strong>横按 vs 拇指扣弦：</strong>需要饱满封闭和声:
• Barre vs thumb wrap:When you need a full, closed voicing, use a big index-finger (1) barre; when you need right-hand muting plus double-stop hammer-pull ornaments on the top strings (5h7p5), wrap the thumb (T) over the 6th-string root instead.
  • Four-string economy (drop the low end):In band, funk and city pop arranging, deliberately drop the muddy 5th and 6th strings and grab only Drop 2 or 9th/13th voicings on strings 4-3-2-1.
  • Lock onto the magenta signature notes:Playing modally is never about running scales from top to bottom — aim for the magenta signature notes on the fretboard on the strong beats (e.g. ♮6 in Dorian, #4 in Lydian) and you will sound like a master in one second.
<h4>乐句工程：从语音到和声落点 ${levelBadge()}</h4>\n:
Phrase craft: from line to harmonic landing ${levelBadge()}

1. Guide-tone line:Use the 3rd and 7th as your skeleton, land the strong beat of every chord change on the target note, and avoid piling up roots.

2. Enclosure / chromatic approach:Sandwich the target note with the natural note above and the chromatic note below; mind the direction and rhythmic placement of the enclosure.

3. Rhythmic displacement and breathing:Use triplets, dotted values and cross-bar ties to create density contrast; leave 1–2 beats of space at the end of a long phrase for the next chord.

<h4>高水准乐句写作 3 大黄金法则 ${levelBadge()}</h4>:
3 golden rules for strong phrase writing ${levelBadge()}

1. Lock onto the guide tones (3rds and 7ths):On the first beat of each chord change, land on the 3rd or 7th of the target chord — you outline the harmony clearly without ever playing the root.

2. Enclosure and chromatic approach:Before hitting the target note on a strong beat, sandwich it with the natural note above and the chromatic note below to get that lively, grainy sparkle typical of jazz and the Romantic era.

3. Rhythmic contrast and space:Avoid mechanical, even-eighth-note running throughout; try triplets (/8t), dotted values (/4.) and cross-bar ties (~) to create breathing contrast.

<h4>写一句好听的旋律 ${levelBadge()}</h4>\n:
Write a melody that sings ${levelBadge()}

1. Change notes with the chord first:In each bar, find the two most important notes in the chord and keep the melody close to them.

2. Use steps as bridges:Between two notes that sit further apart, walk through the neighbouring notes instead of jumping — it sounds better.

3. Leave some space:Do not fill every beat; long notes and rests make the line sound more like speech.
